approved: The Diverted Profits Tax Bill 2017 imposes a 40% penalty tax on multinationals diverting Australian profits to low-tax offshore related parties lacking economic substance, aiming to reduce tax avoidance and speed up ATO dispute resolution.

The government's bill hides a $50 billion tax cut for big banks and multinationals behind a weak approach to multinational tax avoidance, raising only $200 million. Labor supports the bill but calls for an explanation, and notes its own proposals would raise $1.6 billion over the forward estimates.

The speaker argued for the Treasury Laws Amendment (Combating Multinational Tax Avoidance) Bill 2017 and the Diverted Profits Tax Bill 2017, which impose a 40% penalty rate on diverted profits and increase penalties for large multinationals (e.g., up to $525,000 for late lodgement). The laws are expected to claw back $2 billion in tax this financial year, raise $200 million over forward estimates, and have already prompted Facebook and Google to restructure their Australian tax arrangements.
